diagram_candidates.why: The definition explicitly distinguishes the finite-module vector dual from projective Hom duality and states their shift-reversing involutivity.
diagram_candidates.draw_or_check: Two side-by-side constructions: M ↦ DψM=Hom_k(M,k), with (af)(m)=f(ψ(a)m), and projective P ↦ P#=Hom_B(P,B) with ψ-twisted action; mark internal shifts reverse, Dψ²M≅M and (P#)#≅P on projectives. Clearly keep the domains distinct.

diagram_candidates.why: The definition tracks two distinct Grothendieck groups, two forgetful maps, and a Cartan homomorphism across blockwise Hecke/KLR equivalences.
diagram_candidates.draw_or_check: Parallel K₀ᵍʳ(HΛ) and G₀ᵍʳ(HΛ) columns mapping by φ to corresponding RΛ groups; vertical Cartan c maps projective to module classes, horizontal/descending ζ maps each to its ungraded counterpart. Mark q-shifts preserved; keep K₀ and G₀ as separate nodes.
diagram_candidates.classification: Optional, source-supported enhancement; no confirmed visual error.

diagram_candidates.why: The proof moves from joint generalized residue projectors to sums by total residue content and then to a direct sum of central ideals.
diagram_candidates.draw_or_check: For each residue sequence ν, show e(ν) projecting to its generalized-residue space; group sequences with common content α into eα=Σcontent(ν)=α e(ν); conclude H=⊕α eαH. Label eα central, orthogonal, summing to 1, while explicitly marking “may be zero; not asserted primitive.”
diagram_candidates.classification: Optional, source-supported enhancement; no confirmed visual error.

diagram_candidates.why: The theorem presents paired identifications from projective and simple Grothendieck groups to the lower and upper global bases, respectively.
